language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
Hola, Hi, my name is Rafe! This is my Papa, Alonso. We live on a farm in Andalucia Spain where we grow many types of fruits, but mainly olives and oranges.
Papa wants to make sure I understand information in line graphs and that I can also create a line graph.
One graph we use is to show how much the olive trees have grown over the years.
Let’s look at that graph while Papa explains it.
The horizontal ( ) part of every line graph is called the x-axis. The vertical ( ) part of a line graph is called the y-axis.
We use a labels to identify what the information on both axis represents.
Be sure to use scales with logical increments (step by a set numbers like 5, 10, 100).
Last, it is important to have a graph title. The graph title is listed at the top of the graph.
After the title, x and y axis labels and scales are listed, it is time to plot the points on the graph
Each point is marked on the graph at the intersection of the x and y axis.
Here is the table of information that was used to plot the points on the graph.
Can you see where each point is plotted?
A line graph shows where a two numbers meet on graph. All of the points on the graph are connected together to show how something changes over time.
